reason: Lobes or parts that 'spread out' are spreading, as 'patent' was mapped (C224). The glomerule example ('± spread out') is closer to loose, but it is the minority reading.

Margins fringed with hairs that happen to be stellate. The margin quality is ciliate, which the union-pair reviews already ground to PATO_0001408. The hair form is too rare (3 statements) to justify a class like stellate-lepidote.
'sub-' means nearly: the approximate-value pattern applied to square.

target: new: quality of a region of the part (distal portion; dilated PATO_0001571)
reason: The widening holds of the distal region of the pedicel, petiole or style, not of the whole part. 'Expanded' was mapped to dilated (C181), but no class or pattern covers the distal portion.
A comparison with another part whose second term is cut off, as 'similar' was rejected (C245).
A rhomboid outline that is broader than long, as in pine cone apophyses. Record it as rhomboid plus a width-greater-than-length ratio rather than adding a term.
Filaments widened, usually at the base, into a triangular expansion. The quality is dilated (as rule C181 'expanded filament base'). The triangular outline of the widened part is secondary.
Trunk is a synonym of stem in PO. 'Trunkless' palms lack an aerial trunk (acaulescent), the same form as 'leafless' in pattern 15.

target: new: hyphenated compound of two values (panicle-like FLOPO:0991198 of umbel-like units FLOPO:0991031)
reason: A compound inflorescence: a panicle whose last branches end in umbels. These are two values at two levels of branching, not one quality.
A scale or phyllary of uniform width has parallel sides.
PATO_0001946 banded has the synonym striped, so unstriped is its negation, as 'unlobed' is (C239).
Weblike venation is a network of veins, which is the definition of FLOPO reticulate.
A fragment of 'with or without purple or bluish ...' whose noun (tinge, spots) is cut off. Purple itself is already grounded.
Arcuate venation means secondary veins that curve upwards before reaching the margin, the definition of camptodromous. Classic examples like Cornus are eucamptodromous, its child.
A likeness to a taxon without a stated character: jointed, hollow, tall or woody. It is too vague to ground, unlike the defined palm-like habit.

label: cap-shaped
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a cap: a low dome, convex outside and hollow beneath, fitting over the end of another structure. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991248 mitrate (a taller, conical hood) and PATO:0002227 cup-shaped.
reason: A cap-shaped caruncle, as in Euphorbiaceae, is a recognised seed character, and no PATO or FLOPO class has this low-dome shape.
Sand adhering to the roots (a rhizosheath) has no PO class and depends on the habitat. 'Sometimes' marks it as an inconstant condition rather than a quality of the root.
Same reading as 'coated in sand'.
A raceme whose lower pedicels lengthen to bring the flowers to a flat top, i.e. a corymb-like inflorescence.

word: covered with remains of leaf sheaths
reason: The statement is about the old leaf sheaths, which wither but stay on the stem. Annotate the sheath as marcescent rather than adding a stem quality.
A transcription fragment: the covering (hairs, scales) is the quality and is cut off, as 'covered' was rejected (C240).

label: crenate-serrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing forward-pointing teeth that are rounded rather than sharp at their tips. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991256 spinose-serrate; intermediate between PATO:0001206 serrated and PATO:0001889 scalloped.
reason: A standard margin term naming one kind of tooth, not two alternatives. It follows the precedent of spinose-serrate as a child of serrated.

target: new: colour of a marking (spotted PATO_0000333, spots crimson)
reason: Two values: the part is spotted, and the spots, not the part, are crimson. This needs a pattern that gives the colour of a marking rather than a term.

label: crownshaft-forming
definition: A structural quality inhering in a leaf or whole plant by virtue of the leaves' tubular, closed sheaths enclosing one another to form a smooth, conspicuous column at the top of the trunk below the blades. NOTE: Botany-specific (Arecaceae); presupposes FLOPO:0991105 sheathing.
reason: The crownshaft is a key character in palm keys. There is no PO class for it to use as an entity_presence rule, and 'sheathing' alone does not imply it.
A spelling variant of the existing class.

target: new: hyphenated compound of two values (triangular PATO_0001875 / ovate FLOPO:0991024 / orbicular PATO_0001934)
reason: A shape intermediate between three named shapes. Annotate it with the hyphenated-compound pattern, not a term.
A fragment of 'densely several- to many-flowered': an indefinite count of flowers plus a dense arrangement (PATO_0001164).

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (plant organ base FLOPO_0985024 + dentated PATO_0001205)
reason: The scales have a denticulate base. The bearer is the base of the scale (rule C267) and the quality is toothed.
Both values hold at once: an obpyramidal body flattened from above. Two records on the same bearer, with no new term.
An equality or comparison of length with the perianth, joined as alternatives (patterns 09 and 07).
